title: [CQ-C11] Context integration and hardening
description:
Objective: Verify stale context, new helpers, incomplete semantic analysis, session deltas and recipe mismatch across roles.

Deliverable: Context integration and hardening. This is task C11 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): C10.
definitionOfDone: Zero planner calls occur only for valid reuse/eligible recipe paths.
No approval or scope boundary is bypassed.

taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.

implementationPlan.note:
Inventory (no code). Every prerequisite is landed and exposes what the matrix needs; nothing is missing, so no block.

Landed names the tests call:
- C02/C02b: readRepositorySource(root, commit, queries, opts) and readSnapshotSource(snapshot, {commit, base?, overlay?}, queries). Snapshots come from scripts/local-runner/source-export.mjs exportSourceSnapshot({repoDir, commit}).
- C03: readSemanticSource(root, commit, queries, {serenaPath, ...}). A missing absolute serenaPath gives 'semantic-unavailable:analyzer-absent' + inconclusive + a C02 fallback.
- C04: SourceCache, cachedRepositorySource, cachedSnapshotSource, cachedSemanticSource.
- C05: recordNegative(cache, q, result, gen), lookupNegative(cache, q, gen), snapshotScopeGeneration and repositoryScopeGeneration.
- C06/C06a: getContextTool handler {sessionId, basePacketId, contextEpoch}. servedContext.contextDelta is {served:'delta'} or {served:'full', reason}; unrecorded reads take their receiptStatus as the reason.
- C07: claim_next_task and get_context `planReuse`; awaitingPlanReuse and ensurePlanReuseAssessment; settlePlanReuseAssessments(state).
- C08: instantiateRecipe(state, {taskId, recipeId, inputs}), recipeKinds, readRecipeInstance and RECIPE_DEFINITIONS_PATH. RECIPE_ACTOR is exported from tools/submitPlan.ts, not recipe.ts.
- C09: docsLiteralReplace.assessPostpatch(root, {taskId, instance, definition, postCommit}). Importing the module registers the kind.
- C11a: docs.

Deviation, landed contract wins: the plan listed C07 'refresh' (an affected file changed) as needing a planner. Landed C07 and its design (decision-cq-c07-plan-reuse-split) resume BOTH reuse and refresh to WORKING. Refresh is the approved plan reused, with changedPaths served to the worker. The planner-required cases are therefore reassess, replan (entry from WORKING/REVIEW), a DoD or contract change (planRevision advances, giving approval-not-current), and every recipe fallback. The tests assert this.

Dirty paths from other sessions are left untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
Write packages/moe-daemon/src/__e2e__/plannerBoundaries.e2e.test.ts for DoD2 and DoD3. A planner call is counted as an architect claim_next_task({statuses:['PLANNING']}) that returns the task.

Zero planner calls occur ONLY on these paths:
- (a) C07 reuse. The plan is approved, the row re-enters PLANNING from BACKLOG, and an unrelated commit lands. The row resumes WORKING with approvedPlanRevision unchanged and never re-stamped, and the architect claim never returns it.
- (b) An eligible C09 recipe through instantiateRecipe under TURBO. The row reaches WORKING with zero architect claims.

A planner is REQUIRED (the claim returns the task, with the reason visible in planReuse or the fallback system message) for:
- C07 refresh or reassess: an affected file changed, or an anchor or assumption changed;
- C07 replan: entry from WORKING or REVIEW;
- every recipe fallback.

Approval and scope boundaries (DoD3):
- A CONTROL recipe instantiation stays AWAITING_APPROVAL with no approvedPlanRevision.
- SPEED approves only after its delay.
- A DoD or contract change advances planRevision, so the row is not reused.
- The 'moe-recipe' identity is NOT_ALLOWED for an MCP caller, and a forged recipeInstance is stripped.
- assessPostpatch refuses extra edits.
- A delta never crosses a session or attempt boundary.
implementationPlan.note:
New file: src/__e2e__/plannerBoundaries.e2e.test.ts (140 lines, 15 tests). Both e2e files total 363 lines, under the 400 cap.

A planner call is counted by plannerCalls(): up to two ranked architect claim_next_task({statuses:['PLANNING']}) calls, each followed by settlePlanReuseAssessments. It records whether either call returned task-1.

C07 (real TURBO submit_plan with an approved plan, then re-enter PLANNING):
- Z1, 0 planner calls:
  - an unrelated commit gives reuse;
  - an affected file changed gives refresh, with changedPaths ['src/a.ts'] served to the worker claim.
  - In both, planRevision, approvedPlanRevision, planApprovedAt, planSubmittedAt, the plan and the contract are unchanged; nothing is re-stamped.
- P1, 1 planner call with the reason:
  - assumption-changed:src/lib/b.ts (reassess);
  - replan-requested-from-WORKING and replan-requested-from-REVIEW;
  - DoD change and contract change, each giving approval-not-current with planRevision +1.
  - In all of these the worker claim gets nothing.

Recipes:
- Z2: an eligible docs-literal-replace under TURBO reaches WORKING with 0 planner calls. affectedFiles and approvedScope are exactly ['docs/a.md'], and the instance is bound to this revision.
- P2: five fallbacks (hash-mismatch, path-not-allowed, old-text-missing, recipe-not-found, definitions-missing). Each posts the notice, leaves the row untouched (rev 0, no plan, no instance, no approval) and gives 1 planner call.
- B1: CONTROL stays AWAITING_APPROVAL with no approval, 0 planner calls and no worker claim. SPEED (300ms) is still unapproved at 50ms, then approves the same revision.
- B2: a wire workerId 'moe-recipe' gets NOT_ALLOWED. A forged recipeInstance through updateTask is stripped (and reads null).

Extra-edit refusal and delta boundaries are covered in contextInvalidation R2 and D1-D7 (named in the file header).

Runs (Linux snapshot):
- __e2e__ dir: 48/48 pass.
- Scratch-tsconfig tsc over both test files: exit 0.

Mutants: 12 run, all killed after one test fix. The killed set:
- withhold disabled; assumption made soft; refresh made reassess; REVIEW dropped from REPLAN_FROM;
- DoD revision bump off; contract revision bump off; resume re-stamps planApprovedAt;
- reserved guard off; recipeInstance strip off; CONTROL auto-approves; hash check off;
- SPEED delay 0. This one first SURVIVED; I fixed B1 to observe the row mid-delay and it is now killed, while the unmutated baseline stays green.

No prerequisite defect was found, so step 4 has nothing to fix.

implementationPlan.description:
Fix forward, only where the e2e tests expose a real defect in a prerequisite.
- Make the smallest fix in the owning module. Call moe.declare_files on it first, and keep or add a regression in the e2e file.
- Never weaken an assertion, and never work around a defect inside a test.
- A fix over about 30 lines, or one that changes a contract, gets moe.report_blocked naming the owning task instead.
- Error handling must stay fail-closed.
- Record every fix, with its owning task, in the step note.
implementationPlan.note:
No prerequisite defect was exposed, so no fix was made to any owning module. I did not call declare_files: there are no non-test edits.

New test B3 in plannerBoundaries.e2e.test.ts (+10 lines; the file is now 150 and the two files 373, under 400):
- The approved plan is requeued and an unrelated commit lands.
- The assessment's Git is held, and the ranked architect claim returns hasNext:false.
- The architect then makes an explicit claim_next_task {taskId, statuses:['PLANNING']} and gets the row.
- On release, the late reuse result must write nothing: the row stays PLANNING, assigned to architect-1, with no planReuse.

The still-pending clause stays untested. QA judged it effectively unreachable (dedupe plus a single writer).

comments.content:
Docs and integration hand-forward from CQ-C01 (task-fef5ca57, plan rev 1). Verify against what landed before writing anything.

Default and full get_context task reads gain `packetManifest`:
- `version`.
- `provenance`: task {id, planRevision}, epic, project, and candidate (when one exists).
- `sections`: entries {path, mandatory, status (C02's served|truncated|omitted|missing), reason, count}.
  - MANDATORY_SECTIONS are never role-trimmed or truncated.
  - Omissions are explicit: role-trim, compacted comments/chat, capped commits/siblings/rejections.
- `complete`.
- `limitations`, sorted. 'no-repository-source' stays until C10 serves C02's provider.
- `budget`: {limitChars, mandatoryChars, status within|overflow, requirement expand|restructure}.

There is also a new optional `packetBudgetChars` input (1000..250000, default 100000), refused when invalid, never clamped.

The manifest sits inside F06's packetId digest and never grants approval.

For C11, document all of this in docs/MCP_SERVER.md (get_context) and docs/SCHEMA.md. C06 (deltas) and C10 (targeted guidance) build on these section paths and codes.
